canonical_name: Integrated IS-IS for IP and OSI (RFC 1195)
parent_family: OSI IS-IS / Integrated IS-IS interior-routing lineage
roles: provide link-state/SPF interior routing for IP
support OSI and IP in one integrated routing protocol
addressing: Extends the OSI IS-IS routing environment with IP-specific reachability while retaining IS-IS routing-domain/area hierarchy.
routing_or_forwarding: Dynamic link-state routing using SPF/Dijkstra; supports pure-IP, pure-OSI and dual environments as specified in RFC 1195.

operations.monitoring: Operational management is external to the core protocol; RFC 1195 notes management MIB work separately.
operations.diagnostics: Adjacency, LSP database, Level 1/Level 2 topology and IP/OSI reachability are key operational states.
operations.failure_behavior: Link-state database changes are flooded and SPF recomputation updates routes; exact timers and implementation behavior require version-specific records.
operations.operator_interface: Area/domain boundaries and IP/OSI capability are administratively configured.

survival.provenance_notes: IS-IS remains a major routing protocol; repository focus is the historical OSI→integrated-IP lineage.

open_questions: Recover ISO 10589 edition history and compare with RFC 1142 representation.
Identify first operational IP-only or dual Integrated IS-IS deployments.
Trace early vendor implementations and configuration syntax.
Build extension genealogy for later wide metrics, multi-topology and IPv6 support.

sources.notes: Parent protocol source; RFC 1195 is the direct IP integration specification.

related_artifacts.notes: RFC 1195 explicitly bases integrated IP/OSI routing on the OSI Intra-domain IS-IS protocol with IP-specific additions.
OSPF and Integrated IS-IS are parallel link-state IGP families, not formal revisions of one another.

notes: This artifact is a key example of a protocol crossing from the OSI standards ecosystem into operational IP routing rather than being replaced by an Internet-native design.
